correctness.rationale: For every admissible mean-one marginal supported in [0,L], the positive two-point mixing kernel (b-a)nu(da)nu(db)/m plus the atom at one exactly reconstructs the law. Independence preserves convex mixing of the target event. The four possible elementary success patterns are exhaustive: no HH, HH only, one cross, or both crosses. HH-only probabilities <=1/[L(3-L)] for 3/2<=L<=2 and <=1/2 for L>=2; one cross <=1/2; both crosses reduce to H(A,B) monotone on [0,min(1,L-2)]^2 and maximal H(t,t), with H(t,t)-1/2=(2t^2-1)/(2(1+2t)^2). If L<3/2 the event is impossible. Explicit admissible elementary laws attain all five branches, including inclusive boundary cases. The bundled exact-rational checker successfully completed 32397 finite assertions; finite checks are supporting calculations, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: A common support cap is a natural, empirically available condition when controlling the same upper-tail event that Ling/Feige/Samuels study under first moments alone. Its precise effect is neither a routine substitution nor a known-table lookup: the full exact five-regime envelope has a discontinuous onset at cap 3/2, a nontrivial plateau to 2+1/sqrt(2), and a structural optimizer switch from asymmetric high-high to a deterministic single-coordinate mechanism to symmetric at-least-one-high. This answers the natural quantitative question of how boundedness sharpens an otherwise sharp moment-only extremum, without assuming a downstream theorem or falsely claiming an all-n result.
